clean_story:
"Machines with senses. Tasks without fatigue.
The word robotics comes from 'robota,' meaning forced labor, as these machines perform work humans cannot or will not.

A robotic arm in a car factory welds seams with precision measured in thousandths of an inch, repeating the same motion every 12 seconds for years. A drone maps farmland, using cameras to spot sick plants by their color, like a farmer with an eagle’s eyes. These machines don’t tire, don’t blink, and don’t forget instructions. Their strength lies in repetition and accuracy, turning raw materials into products or data into decisions. Yet they rely on humans for programming, maintenance, and purpose—tools, not replacements.

Three related subjects are automation, artificial intelligence and human machine collaboration."
